chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Supplication remains veiled/barred until blessings are sent upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.
ai.seo_question: Why is my supplication not accepted?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the necessity of Salawat as a spiritual prerequisite for the acceptance of supplication, linking the intercessory status of the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt to the efficacy of the believer's prayers. Scholars often interpret 'mahjub' (veiled) not merely as a rejection, but as a temporary concealment due to the lack of this essential spiritual currency, emphasizing the unique role of the Ahl al-Bayt as mediators of divine grace.
